- **M1** (2026-08-29T17:41:32.937Z) — Record-hygiene D1 exempts a Bash call only when EVERY shell segment leads with git or sofar. Decorating a git command with echo labels — the common `echo "=== status ===" && git status` habit — breaks the exemption, so the PostToolUse hook appends a command_run event and the tree is dirty again the instant it was clean. This is exactly the loop D1 was written to break, and it is easy to re-enter by accident right after a write-back, where the trailing event lands after session_ended and forces an amend. Convention: once you have written back, run git and sofar commands BARE and chained only to each other (`git add <paths> && git commit --amend --no-edit`), with no echo, no comments and no pipes to head. Use echo decoration freely before the write-back, never after it.
